title: Detection of endogenous circadian rhythms of clock gene mRNA expression in mouse lung tissue using slice cultures
protocol: Add FBS to the basal tissue slice culture media at a ratio of 1:10.
Dispense the FBS-supplemented culture media at 1.8 mL per non-treated 35 mm dish.
Dispense the basal culture media at 1.8 mL per 35 mm dish for washing.
Put the inserts in the dishes with media for pre-culture (no need for washing and re-culture).
Prepare tools for dissection.
Wipe scissors, tweezers, razor blade, and syringe with 70% ethanol.
Fill 35 mm glass Petri dishes with ice-cold HBSS containing 1% HEPES.
Place Petri dishes on ice.
Wash dissected tissue twice, once in each glass dish filled with HBSS containing 1% HEPES.
Cut rods from the lung on a cutting stage moistened with HBSS supplemented with 1% HEPES.
Float the slices in HBSS (+1% HEPES) in the third glass dish.
Place dishes with inserts on ice.
Put a 10 mm plastic culture dish on ice upside down, place a circular filter paper over it, and moisten it with HBSS (+1% HEPES).
Set up the chopping machine (McIlwain, Cat# 51350) with thickness set to 300 μm.
Attach a blade to the holder, wipe it with 70% ethanol using a cotton swab.
Layer two sheets of filter paper on the circular stainless-steel table.
Adjust the angle of the blade arm by test cutting weighing paper until cut lines are visible in the center portion of the stage.
Administer anesthesia inhalation (isoflurane) to the mouse.
Euthanize the mouse by cervical dislocation.
Spray the mouse with 70% ethanol.
Incise the skin from the abdomen to the ribcage using scissors.
Cut the muscle to expose the abdominal cavity and organs.
Dissect the lung and wash it in ice-cold HBSS containing 1% HEPES.
Place the dissected lung on the cutting stage.
Cut out a thin rod of tissue (1–2 mm width) from the edge of the lung with a razor blade.
Place the tissue sample on sterilized weighing paper.
Place the specimen on the circular stainless-steel table of the chopping machine.
Fix the weighing paper with your fingers during cutting.
Slide off the sliced lung from the weighing paper using the side of the needle.
Float the slice in ice-cold HBSS (+1% HEPES) solution.
Transfer slices one by one onto the handmade culture insert so they do not overlap.
Handle slices gently with round-tipped tweezers to avoid damage.
Place slices from one rod randomly on each insert.
Observe each slice under a stereomicroscope.
Spread folded slices out with the tip of a syringe needle.
Seal sample dishes with parafilm.
Incubate sealed dishes at 37°C in an incubator.
Harvest samples for time point 0 before initiating DEX stimuli.
Prepare medium for washing and re-culture by placing it in an incubator at 37°C the day before use.
Dispense medium to room temperature (20°C–30°C) if prepared the previous day.
Incubate dispensed medium at 37°C before use.
Place dishes containing medium for washing and re-culture in an incubator at 37°C a few hours before starting DEX stimuli.
Remove the samples from the incubator.
Pipette 500 μL of medium from the culture in the 1.5 mL test tube containing DEX.
Return the mixture of media and DEX to the dish and swirl softly (final concentration: 100 nM).
Incubate the samples for 1 h at 37°C.
Transfer the inserts into dishes containing washing media.
Place the inserts in dishes with re-culture medium, seal the dishes with parafilm, and restart incubation.
Harvest lung slices at designated times (2 days total).
Dispense 300 μL of RLT buffer into the 1.5 mL test tubes equipped with a BioMasher II.
Open the insert frame to remove the membrane containing the slice.
Open the frame using round-tipped tweezers.
Peel off the membrane with the slice carefully.
Trim the membrane with scissors to fit the diameter of the test tube, avoiding the slice.
Soak the membrane into RLT buffer.
Scrape the slice from the membrane using a 200 μL pipette tip.
Homogenize lung tissue using BioMasher II approximately 30–50 times.
Store the lysate samples at −80°C until RNA extraction step.
Pass the lysate through a QIAshredder (Qiagen) for complete homogenization.
Extract RNA from the lung lysate using an RNeasy Mini Kit following manufacturer’s instructions.
Measure the concentration of extracted RNA in a spectrophotometer.
Perform reverse transcription to prepare complementary DNA (cDNA).
Dilute purified RNA with dH2O to obtain a solution of 1.5 μg of RNA.
Prepare diluted cDNA samples by adding 80 μL dH2O to 20 μL of reverse transcription reaction solution.
Dilute known amounts of vector cloning the cDNA of clock genes for standards in a 5-point 10-fold serial dilution ranging from 5 fg/μL to 50 pg/μL.
Prepare a 5-point 10-fold serial standard for 18S-rRNA with a range from 50 fg/μL to 500 pg/μL.
Dispense 20 μL of the master mix into each well of a 96-well plate.
Add 5 μL of diluted cDNA to each well.
Mix well by pipetting on ice.
Check the wells for bubbles after adding cDNA.
Move any bubbles in the liquid to the surface by lightly tapping the bottom of the well.
Seal the 96-well plate.
Set the sealed plate in the real-time PCR detection system.
Run the RT-qPCR reaction.
